occurrences.source_excerpt: How to fit a Wheelchair? • Seat width (#3) This is the width of the back-side when sitting on a flat surface (+ 1-2 inches) • Seat Depth (C) Make this measurements by measuring from back of buttock to inside of Patient is in 90°-90°-90° sitting position with spine neutral knee. • Back height (B) Measure this from the top of the shoulders down to the bottom of the back- side when sitting on a flat surface. Seat-to-Floor Height (D) This is important if the patient is going to propel the wheelchair

occurrences.source_excerpt: Safety tips for using wheelchair ➢ Always LOCK the brakes when you leave the patient or when not being pushed. ➢ Avoid leaning forwards or bending to reach low objects ➢ Never stand on the footplates ➢ Use safety straps if provided (especially when going outdoors or for patient with poor sitting balance) ➢ Make sure: ➢ Feet safely on the footplates ➢ Elbows, all clothing, rugs or bags are tucked in safely. ➢ Always let the client know what you are going to do

source_pages.source_file: 12 - 4. Transfer techniques and standard wheelchairs 轉移技巧及輪椅使用.pdf
source_pages.formatted: 12 - 4. Transfer techniques and standard wheelchairs 轉移技巧及輪椅使用.pdf, slide 32 (PDF p. 32)

occurrences.source_excerpt: Using the wheelchair - Getting into the wheelchair • LOCK the brakes! • Fold up the footplates and swing sway. • Stand with back of leg against the seat and press down on armrest. • Lower and place foot on footplates. • Pay attention to keep the heel clear of the front casters. Getting out of the wheelchair • LOCK the brakes! • Fold up the footplates and swing sway. • Make sure walking aids(if needed) is ready. • Slightly bend trunk forwards, standing up by pressing down on the armrest

occurrences.source_excerpt: Safety tips for using wheelchair ➢ Always LOCK the brakes when you leave the patient or when not being pushed. ➢ Avoid leaning forwards or bending to reach low objects ➢ Never stand on the footplates ➢ Use safety straps if provided (especially when going outdoors or for patient with poor sitting balance) ➢ Make sure: ➢ Feet safely on the footplates ➢ Elbows, all clothing, rugs or bags are tucked in safely. ➢ Always let the client know what you are going to do

occurrences.source_excerpt: Conditions with Precautions Total hip replacement (THR) OR dislocated hip • DON’T place affected side in Cross leg position (flex+ adducted+ medial rotated) OR flexion > 90° 90° • maintain affected side in semi- reclining position & abduction during side transfer • Use of abduction pillow if prescribed • Especially within the first 2 weeks after surgery

occurrences.source_excerpt: Using the wheelchair - Getting into the wheelchair • LOCK the brakes! • Fold up the footplates and swing sway. • Stand with back of leg against the seat and press down on armrest. • Lower and place foot on footplates. • Pay attention to keep the heel clear of the front casters. Getting out of the wheelchair • LOCK the brakes! • Fold up the footplates and swing sway. • Make sure walking aids(if needed) is ready. • Slightly bend trunk forwards, standing up by pressing down on the armrest

Spinal cord injury

rolling the entire body

Using the wheelchair - Getting up slope
➢ Facing towards the slope
➢ Keep back straight and use lower limbs muscles
➢ ‘Z’ shape
Getting down a slope
➢ Facing towards the slope and guided the wheelchair backwards slowly

occurrences.source_excerpt: Standard Wheelchair - Postural Support Options 1. Seats 1. • sling/ rigid • +/- wheelchair cushions/ pelvic strap 2. Backs: sling/ rigid/ recline 2. 3. Arm rests: • fixed / removeable • 3. • Properly positioned armrest not only provide support to the upper body but also decrease the weight on the buttocks by 5% for individuals with tetraplegia to 9% for individuals with paraplegia.
